summary: This note describes Harvard Law School, one of the professional graduate schools of Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It is presented as the oldest continually operating law school in the United States and as one of the most prestigious in the world. The note focuses on its selectivity and rankings, including its acceptance rate, yield rate, and comparisons with Yale and Stanford.
one_line: Harvard Law School, the founded-1817 graduate law school of Harvard University, described by its ranking, admissions selectivity, and yield rate.
key_facts: Harvard Law School is one of the professional graduate schools of Harvard University, located in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
Harvard Law School was founded in 1817.
Harvard Law School is the oldest continually operating law school in the United States.
Harvard Law School is generally considered to be one of the most prestigious law schools in the world.
The school is ranked third by U.S. News & World Report.
Harvard Law School's acceptance rate was 15.4% in the 2013-14 admissions cycle.
Harvard Law School's yield rate of 66.2% was the second-highest of any law school in the United States.
Harvard Law School is ranked first in the 2016 QS World University Rankings.
Harvard Law admitted 16.5% of applicants in its most recent class.
Yale admitted 9.2% of applicants in the comparison class cited in the note.
Stanford admitted 11.2% of applicants in the comparison class cited in the note.
Harvard Law School is also known as Harvard Law or HLS.
